CMV , Herpes simplex\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E##How alcohol causes vomiting ??\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThrowing up or vomiting after drinking alcohol is the body’s natural way of removing potentially harmful material.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhen the body processes alcohol, the liver converts it into a highly reactive, toxic chemical called acetaldehyde.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAcetaldehyde can cause tissue damage and may trigger the onset of health conditions. The liver then converts the acetaldehyde into acetate, which the body can remove by converting it to water and carbon dioxide.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHowever, the liver can only process a certain amount of acetaldehyde at a time. If the acetaldehyde levels are higher than the liver can convert, the body will remove the excess chemical by vomiting.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe liver can only process a certain amount of acetaldehyde. If the level of acetaldehyde is higher than the liver can process, the body will react by vomiting to get rid of the excess chemicals. Accordingly, excessive alcohol consumption can be the cause of vomiting after drinking alcohol.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis high rate of elimination of toxic chemicals can be due to a high level of activity from enzyme systems.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDrinking alcohol can also cause a person’s stomach to produce more acid than it would typically. This acid buildup can irritate and erode the stomach lining, causing mucosal inflammation known as gastritis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr
